'''Docking:''' {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Sheila Frahm]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Sam Brownback]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsKS}} The '''1996 United States Senate special election in Kansas''' was held on November 5, 1996, concurrently with the [[1996 United States presidential election|presidential election]] and the regularly scheduled [[1996 United States Senate election in Kansas|election]] for the state's Class 2 seat. Incumbent Republican U.S. Senator and Senate Majority Leader [[Bob Dole]], the Republican nominee for president, had resigned on June 11, 1996, in order to focus on [[Bob Dole 1996 presidential campaign|his presidential campaign]]. Lieutenant Governor [[Sheila Frahm]] was appointed to the seat upon Dole's resignation, but she was defeated in the primary by Representative [[Sam Brownback]], who went on to win the general election over Democrat Jill Docking. Brownback served in the U.S. Senate from 1996 to 2011 and later as governor of Kansas from 2011 to 2018; in his successful [[2014 Kansas gubernatorial election|2014]] gubernatorial re-election campaign, he defeated the Democratic ticket, which included Docking as the nominee for lieutenant governor. As of 2025, this is the last time a Democratic candidate won [[Cowley County, Kansas|Cowley County]] as well as [[Ellis County, Kansas|Ellis County]] in a US Senate election. ==Republican primary== In [[2010 Kansas gubernatorial election|2010]], Brownback was elected [[Governor of Kansas|governor]], and won a second term [[2014 Kansas gubernatorial election|in 2014]]. He resigned as governor on January 31, 2018, to accept an ambassadorship, and was succeeded by Lieutenant Governor [[Jeff Colyer]]. Brownback's seat is now held by [[Jerry Moran]], a U.S. representative from Kansas' 1st district for seven terms (1997–2011).
